note: Questions are paraphrases; distinctive terms are deliberately absent.

probes.question: who prefers meeting us out on site rather than sitting in their office
probes.body: Rang ahead but he was on site so I went out to him, muddy boots job. Good rapport, he likes that we come out to the work rather than sitting in the office.

probes.question: which customer raised nothing at all and we agreed to keep monthly visits
probes.body: No issues raised at all this visit. Just a coffee and a catch up, keep the cadence at monthly.

probes.question: who's gone in for that housing association new build deal that could lift volumes
probes.body: They've registered for the new build framework with the housing association. If it lands it's a step up in volume, worth watching from June.

probes.question: who's started doing their own digging work so we could supply drainage and stone
probes.body: They've started doing more groundworks off their own bat. Opportunity on drainage and MOT type 1 if we can get the haulage right.

probes.question: who's waiting on a price for below ground drainage pipework at Tarvin
probes.body: He wants a quote on 60 lengths of 110 underground pipe plus bends for the Tarvin job. Promised it by Friday.

probes.question: who sticks with one make of sealant but might move on price
probes.body: Discussed the sealant and adhesives lines, they're loyal to one brand but open to a comparison if the price is right.

probes.question: which customer keeps getting asked about car charger fitting and wants our range
probes.body: Talked through EV charging install work, they're getting asked about it more. Not our area really but I said I'd find out what we stock.

probes.question: who's signed up for the supplier day at the branch in the autumn
probes.body: They've booked in for the manufacturer's day at the depot in October. Nia Okafor and two of the lads coming.

probes.question: who's taken on a new pricing person who came from a plumbers merchant
probes.body: New estimator started, Priya Chandran, comes from a plumbing merchant background. Introduced myself, should be a good contact for pricing enquiries.

probes.question: which contracts manager has picked up the second phase of that flats scheme
probes.body: Dave Enright (contracts manager) has taken on the Kirkstall Road flats phase 2, 34 plots, starts mid March. Wants a call on plasterboard and metal stud nearer the time.

probes.question: which customer's doing the warehouse roof and needs the membrane details sent over
probes.body: Site visit at Bury, they're on the roof of a warehouse conversion. Talked single ply and edge trim, sending over spec Thursday.

probes.question: who looked flat out with work on but had nothing to report
probes.body: Nothing to report other than they're busy. Two skips in the yard and a full board of jobs on the wall.

probes.question: where did I leave the new insulation literature and brochures for the trade counter
probes.body: Dropped off the new insulation guide and a stack of catalogues for the counter at their unit.

probes.question: who's steering spend our way to reach the next discount level
probes.body: Talked rebate. He knows he's close to the next threshold and is actively steering spend our way to hit it. Good sign.

probes.question: who did I sort an urgent same day sheet material drop for
probes.body: Asked me for a favour on a one-off, needed 12 sheets of OSB same day. Sorted it through the branch, he was grateful. Bank that.

probes.question: which customer's buying more drill bits and blades since we fixed the stand
probes.body: Been buying more of the power tool accessories since we sorted the display. Small money but it's sticky business.

probes.question: who's reordered the outdoor slabs after the first lot flew out
probes.body: Bought their first pallet of the porcelain paving, sold through in a fortnight. Reordered two more, said the homeowners love the grey.

probes.question: who told me our website's easier to use than their old supplier's
probes.body: He commented that our online ordering is easier than the last lot he used. Small thing but he brought it up unprompted.

probes.question: which customer's grown their van fleet so we may need to rethink drop times
probes.body: Mo Osei mentioned they've taken on two more vans, so delivery windows may need looking at. Nothing urgent but worth flagging to transport.

probes.question: how many boards did I quote for the Ashwell Road flats
probes.body: Quoted 62 sheets of 12.5mm standard board plus scrim and beads for the Ashwell Road flats. Expect the order Thursday.

probes.question: Who's safe enough that I just need to keep in touch and show something new now and then
probes.body: Overall no risk here, just needs regular contact and the odd new line put in front of them. Next visit six weeks.

probes.question: Which customer took away board samples for a couple of garden projects this summer
probes.body: Left samples of the composite decking. Doing a couple of garden jobs in summer, could be a new line for them.

probes.question: Where do I leave the van when I call on the lot above the fish shop
probes.body: Their office is above a chippy on Bridge Street, parking is a nightmare. Note to self, use the Co-op car park and walk round.

probes.question: Whose figures are up again this quarter mostly on the plumbing side
probes.body: Spend up again on last quarter, mostly driven by plumbing. Nothing to fix here, just keep showing up.

probes.question: Who needs a quote back by Friday on graded carcassing for Radcliffe
probes.body: They want a price on 200 lengths of 47x100 C24 for the Radcliffe job. Quote due back by Friday.

probes.question: Which customer won't shift off their paving brand so don't offer alternatives
probes.body: They're loyal to Marshalls on paving, won't be moved. Fine, we supply it anyway, just don't push alternatives.

probes.question: Which contact is a big football fan worth inviting to a corporate day
probes.body: Danny Pike is a Leeds season ticket holder, east stand. Worth an invite to the hospitality day if we get tickets.

probes.question: Where was the visit just a brew and a chat about the weather
probes.body: Nice and relaxed visit, coffee and a moan about the weather. No issues raised at all.

probes.question: Who's abroad for the back half of July and who's covering for her
probes.body: Priya Pike off on holiday to Portugal the last two weeks of July, Gary covering. Don't chase anything in that window.

probes.question: What have I promised to bring to that account when I go back in March
probes.body: Next visit end of March. Bring the tool promo, the portal login sorted, and a price on the Radcliffe timber package.

probes.question: Which visit was rushed because he was stuck on a call the whole time
probes.body: Quick doorstep chat, he was on the phone the whole time. Rebook properly for next month.

probes.question: Who's nearly at their annual rebate target and how much have they got left
probes.body: Reminded him about the loyalty rebate threshold, he's about 8k off it with four months to run. He reckons they'll walk it.

probes.question: Whose other half had an operation earlier this year that I should ask about
probes.body: Ivy Whitfield's wife had a knee operation in January, all fine now. Remember to ask.

probes.question: Who told me they've got another fitter starting with them next week
probes.body: Yard was rammed when I got there, two vans loading at once. Told me they've taken on another fitter starting Monday.

probes.question: Who do I reckon is buying their screws and anchors somewhere local
probes.body: Nice easy visit. Coffee in the portacabin, half an hour of football, no issues raised at all.

probes.question: Which rival keeps calling on them trying to take the drainage work
probes.body: Fixings spend is lower than it should be for their volume. Suspect they're picking up screws and anchors locally, chase it.

probes.question: Who's buying far more fixings than usual and probably stocking their own van
probes.body: Mentioned Cawley and Sons have been in twice this month with a rep chasing the drainage. He wasn't interested but they are sniffing round.

probes.question: Whose civils work is growing quicker than their building work right now
probes.body: Big spend on fixings and consumables this quarter, higher than usual. Suspect they're stocking their own van store rather than buying weekly.

probes.question: When should I ring back about widening out the electrical offer we talked about
probes.body: Groundworks side growing faster than the build side. Chambers, pipe and bedding stone all up.

probes.question: Which visit was just coffee in the site cabin and half an hour of football
probes.body: Talked through the electrical range extension. He'll look at it properly after the bank holiday, said ring him week of the 12th.

probes.question: Did they price that Rochdale education job and when do we hear
probes.body: They quoted a school refurb in Rochdale, find out in three weeks. Would be a decent chunk of plasterboard and metal stud if it lands.

probes.question: Have they taken more staff on this year including any trainees
probes.body: Head count up to 14 from 11 last year. Two new apprentices through the CITB route, both on site with Gary.

probes.question: Who actually raises the orders there and who just approves them
probes.body: Sharon in their office is the one who actually places the orders - Priya Osei just signs things off. Need to build that relationship more, I've been ignoring her.

probes.question: Have we arranged to collect the empty pallets from their yard
probes.body: Asked about pallet returns, they've got about 20 stacked up. Arranged collection with transport for next Tuesday.

probes.question: Has their monthly sheet board usage gone up much on last year
probes.body: Talked timber. They're taking around 40 sheets of 18mm OSB a month now, up from about 25 last year.

probes.question: Are they expecting a slow couple of weeks between jobs soon
probes.body: Quiet fortnight coming as they've a gap between jobs. Expect the order rate to dip briefly then pick up from the 20th.

probes.question: When is the gaffer off on holiday and who covers ordering
probes.body: Alex Marsh away in Lanzarote first two weeks of August. Deal with Sharon or Karl in that window.

probes.question: Do they need anything else for that house extension thats nearly done
probes.body: Extension job on Willow Drive finishing next week, snagging only. Nothing more needed from us on that one.

probes.question: Have I arranged to show him how the web ordering works
probes.body: Talked through the new online ordering portal, he's keen but wants a walkthrough. Booked in for the 22nd, 9am at their office.

probes.question: Does he still rate the rep who had that area before me
probes.body: He knows our rep patch changed and said he liked the old fella, Tony. Building trust from scratch a bit here.

probes.question: What has he got running at Beeston and when does it end
probes.body: He's still got the Beeston care home extension running but it's small beer, two lads on it and it finishes end of April.

probes.question: Is the young lad doing college and who is funding it
probes.body: Ryan the apprentice is doing his level 2 at West Notts, Dave's paying for it himself. Nice detail, ask next visit.

probes.question: Which product lines are actually growing with them right now
probes.body: Fixings and consumables are the only line growing. Suggests they're finishing work, not starting it.

probes.question: Could we push tool hire with him when material sales are slow
probes.body: Talked about the Hilti breaker he hires off us occasionally. Might be worth a hire package to keep him engaged when materials are low.

probes.question: Have they cut back any temporary labour on site lately
probes.body: Sean the foreman was in the yard, said they've laid off one of the agency lads and the other is down to three days.

probes.question: Has he had a tool sat on hire ages without using it
probes.body: They've still got the Hilti breaker on hire from us since August and barely used it. Worth offering to take it back before he asks, would go down well.

probes.question: Do we still get on well even with his workload problems
probes.body: Good rapport still there, he made me a brew and we talked about Forest for twenty minutes. Relationship is fine, it's the workload that's the problem.

probes.question: Have they changed how far ahead they buy their regular materials
probes.body: Karen in the office says they've stopped ordering ahead and are buying week to week now. Worth quoting tighter on the regular lines.

probes.question: What condition is his van in and is he replacing it
probes.body: Van is looking tired, the Transit has done 190k and he said he can't justify changing it yet.

probes.question: Why are those Wharf Lane plots paused and what was he relying on
probes.body: Wharf Lane plots 6 to 9 are on hold until the developer sorts the drainage adoption. That was his bread and butter through the winter.

probes.question: who's bidding on that Sutton education job and when does it close
probes.body: He's tendering for a school refurb in Sutton, closes 12th March. Long shot but I said I'd help with a materials schedule.

probes.question: why has that builder's wood buying grown, have they picked up more plots
probes.body: Their timber usage has gone up if anything, they've won two more housing plots off Barratt. So it's not that the work's dried up.

probes.question: what happened when I offered him a meal or a walk round the job
probes.body: Tried to book a lunch, got a no. Tried a site visit, got a maybe. Not much to work with.

probes.question: which customer's stopped buying since the spring board delivery and won't explain why
probes.body: Third visit running where nobody's ordered anything since the March plasterboard drop. Something's gone wrong and no one will say what.

probes.question: could that autumn price change notice be why the account went silent
probes.body: Quiet since the pricing letter went out in October. I reckon that was the trigger even though nobody's said it outright.

probes.question: did I ever get through when I tried calling him last week
probes.body: Rang Monday, went to voicemail. Rang Thursday, voicemail again. Tried the mobile Friday morning and he picked up then said he was driving.

probes.question: what did the customer do with the product book and billing paperwork I left
probes.body: Left the new catalogue and the account statement. He put both straight in the drawer without looking.

probes.question: does it look like that customer has already made their mind up
probes.body: Feels like they've already decided and are just being polite. Need to give them a reason to reconsider fast.

probes.question: how long did the buyer give me and did he seem interested
probes.body: He was polite, gave me twelve minutes, never once opened his diary. Body language said get on with it.

probes.question: when do I need to get in front of them before that Doncaster education bid
probes.body: They're tendering for the Doncaster school in September. If we're not in front of them by August we're not in it at all.

probes.question: any reply on the fastenings pricing I sent almost a fortnight back
probes.body: Sent quote for the fixings package 12 days ago, no response, no acknowledgement. Chased twice.

probes.question: how many of our metal stock cages are still sitting at their place
probes.body: Still got our stillages in their yard, four of them. He made a point of mentioning it which felt pointed.

probes.question: are we supplying anything on that Kirkstall Road apartment scheme
probes.body: They're on the Kirkstall Road flats job, six blocks, started April. Not a single order off us for it. That hurts.

probes.question: when am I due back there and am I taking something written
probes.body: Diarised to go back in three weeks with a proper written proposal rather than another chat. Last roll of the dice really.

probes.question: did the buyer say he'd use just one merchant if the numbers worked
probes.body: Jordan Pike said outright he'd rather deal with one supplier if the price stacked up. That's the opening, need a proper comparison sheet.

probes.question: which easy switch lines should I go after first with that customer
probes.body: Sealants and adhesives worth attacking first. Low value, low risk for them to switch, gets us on the invoice weekly.

probes.question: any real reason their fastenings order goes to the rival merchant instead of us
probes.body: Asked why the fixings goes to Cawley and Sons and honestly nobody could tell me. Habit, driver knows the trade counter lad, that's about it.

probes.question: who asked about renting a cutting machine for two days in late February
probes.body: Dean asked about hire on a floor saw for two days end of Feb. Passed to the hire desk, need to chase.

probes.question: which bagged materials do we already hold with no competition risk
probes.body: Powder products, sand and cement, plaster, all ours and no threat there as far as I can see.

probes.question: why are they nervous about leaving tools on the Thornhill Grange job
probes.body: Site cabin at Thornhill Grange got broken into over Christmas, lost a couple of Makitas. They're twitchy about leaving anything on site now.
